summary: GiftCookie is a subclass of Cookie that adds gift-wrapping behavior: it reuses everything a Cookie already knows (like its flavor) and layers on small private steps for boxing, tying a ribbon, and attaching a note.

lines.text: The extends keyword makes GiftCookie a kind of Cookie, so it inherits Cookie's fields and methods and only has to describe what is different about a gift cookie.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so GiftCookie declares its own that accepts the flavor a caller wants.
This hands the flavor up to the Cookie constructor so the inherited part of the object is initialized before anything else happens.
This is the one public entry point for wrapping a cookie; callers use it and never need to know how many steps are involved.
Calling a helper method by name keeps this method readable as a list of steps rather than a wall of printing code.
The note the caller supplied is passed along to the helper that actually attaches it.
Returning a confirmation string lets the calling program report success, instead of the class deciding how to announce it.
Marking the helper private hides it from the rest of the program, so packaging steps can only run in the correct order through packageCookie.

lines.code: System.out.println("Packaged " + getFlavor() + " cookie in a box.");
lines.text: getFlavor() is inherited from Cookie, which shows how a subclass reads the parent's data through the parent's own method.
The backslash before each quotation mark is an escape sequence that puts a literal double quote in the output, wrapping the note in quotes.
